summary.tldr: Creates Criminal Code offences for making, selling or advertising commercial pornographic material without checking age and written consent of everyone shown.
what_it_does: Creates an offence for making pornographic material for commercial purposes without first confirming that everyone shown was 18 or older and gave written consent.

Creates an offence for distributing or advertising pornographic material for commercial purposes without written confirmation from the maker about each person’s age, consent and any later written withdrawal of consent.
Sets penalties of up to two years in prison or a $500,000 fine on indictment, or a $100,000 fine on summary conviction.

Presumes a corporation acted for commercial purposes unless it proves otherwise, and limits the age-belief defence unless age was checked with a federal, provincial or foreign ID, or other prescribed document, and it was reasonably believed to be real.
Requires courts to treat a minor’s image, lack of consent to the sexual activity, obscenity, or hate promotion as aggravating factors when sentencing.
Allows courts to ban Internet use, require removal of the material from the Internet or the offender’s computer system, and lets the Governor in Council set ID and record-keeping rules.
